name: kernel_bpf_state
description: Kernel-level residency. eBPF is where BPFDoor- and Symbiote-class implants live, and a memory image alone does not enumerate it cleanly. Nothing is planted here: loading an eBPF program needs privileges the lab deliberately does not grant. What is under test is whether the collection RECORDS the kernel and eBPF state at all — because an analyst cannot review, and a later pass cannot re-derive, evidence that was never captured.

expect.id: eBPF state is collected for offline review
the eBPF hardening posture is recorded
kernel taint is recorded (a loaded LKM is sticky in the taint mask)
